Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (B/B25/B25n0145.xml). Extensive Record of Zhongfeng Mingben of Tianmu. Zhongfeng Mingben owns the retained verse: that fellow cooked up wonders to repay a Chan debt — this land, that west, defeat on defeat; first he met the king of Liang and said 'no knowing', at the last he took Huike's three bows; chill and cold, one sandal returning west — the lacquered bucket still unlightened; a teacher like that, banished to the lion-crag head, mist and cloud locking it a thousand hundred years — just watch whether the brow-hairs rot or not.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J32/J32nB273.xml). Recorded Sayings of Monk Qianyan. Qianyan Yuanzhang owns the retained address at the Founder's remembrance: nine years facing the wall cut off the whole world's tongues; one sandal returning west lost him his own poor life — 'I came to this land' — and still the losing is not finished; 'to hand on the way and save the deluded' — and still the cutting-off is not done; since neither is done nor lost, what, in the end? one flower opens five petals, and the fruit sets of itself.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J25/J25nB155.xml). Recorded Sayings of Elder Wuqu. Wuqu Rukong owns the retained portrait address: wide open and no sage — no true hearer yet; straight-out 'no knowing' — still short of accord; from then on, in the hall of Great Liang, twice he lost his old capital; in the room at Shaolin, nine years of clean ash; at the last, to play the true man, he spared neither flesh, bone, marrow, nor skin — handed his whole body to others, shouldered his staff, one sandal returning west; settled old debts below Bear-Ear peak, played a great wonder on Onion-Ridge head — and was seen through by Song Yun, striding along unsure of high and low; to know the craftsman who builds buddhas and founders — just this sloppy bewhiskered face; all say the Founder left years ago — and the whisk pointed at the portrait: this one right here — say, who is it? then the verse: wide open, no sage — the true mechanism shown; 'no knowing' — the true command lifted again; twice his red heart won no hearing; chill he trod the reeds away down the autumn river.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J39/J39nB447.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Meixi Du of Dongshan. Meixi Fudu owns the retained cremation verse, lighting the fire for the abbot: auspicious wood half-sky flying the north ridge, plum-blossom points opening on the southern sprays — in a flash heaven and earth flip their colors: one sandal returning west — just now.

Senses.Explanation: One sandal, westward home: the tomb opened and holding nothing but a shoe — read at memorials, portraits, installations, and pyres. Zhongfeng Mingben, in the encomium: that fellow cooked up wonders to repay a Chan debt — this land, that west, defeat upon defeat; he met the king of Liang and said 'no knowing', took Huike's three bows; chill and cold, one sandal returning west — the lacquered bucket still unlightened; banished to the lion-crag, mist-locked a thousand years — just watch whether the brow-hairs rot. Qianyan Yuanzhang, at the Founder's remembrance: nine years facing the wall cut off the whole world's tongues; one sandal returning west lost him his own poor life — 'I came to this land', and still the losing is not finished; 'to hand on the way and save the deluded', and still the cutting-off is not done — what, in the end? one flower opens five petals, the fruit sets of itself. Jie'an Jin, as the tablet enters the hall: nine years facing the wall — water rising from the high plain; one sandal returning west — sprouts rising from the ground; and how does the Founder arrive at Jinming? a glance left and right: carrying the bottle, dragging the staff. Guting Shanjian, seeing off a departing master: when Chan reaches the source, waking and delusion cease — the old foreigner's cleverness turned to clumsiness: returning west with one sandal, mud still on it. Wuqu Rukong, before the portrait: wide open, no sage; straight-out, no knowing — twice he lost his old capital in the hall of Liang, nine years of clean ash in the Shaolin room; at the last, a true man spares neither flesh, bone, marrow, nor skin — hands his whole body to others, shoulders the staff, one sandal returning west; old debts settled below Bear-Ear peak, a great wonder played on Onion-Ridge head — seen through by Song Yun — and then the whisk points at the picture: this one right here, who is it?; twice his red heart won no hearing; chill he trod the reeds away down the autumn river. Baishan Dekai, entering his monastery: at the Founder's shrine — the reed crossed the river, that was you; one sandal returning west, that was you; I thought how many tricks — bah, you were only here all along. Meixi Fudu, lighting the pyre: auspicious wood half-sky flying the north ridge, plum-blossom points on the southern sprays — in a flash heaven and earth flip their colors: one sandal returning west — just now.
